"

War thunder, is a "game". It's typically played for suffering, competition, or development of depression.
Now you may think this is one of those "Oh no please don't touch this game I have played it for so long" kind of meme review, but I do actually want to give new players a relatively objective review and viewpoint of the game. I want to note that most of my hours are in air realistic battles, and therefore my comments are ground battles are from what I hear from others.

War thunder is a game that has an extremely long learning curve. The best diagram I can put here would be inserting the "Dunning Krueger Effect" diagram. Your first few hours in the game will be a lot of fun, in fact this will be the most fun you will have in this game. Then you go into realistic battles, and you dip your feet into water that's way too deep or cold than you have anticipated. You're thrown into the world of wild animals where there is no such thing as skill based matchmaking. You will fall quickly into the valley of despair and realize that the game is a lot of pain and suffering.

The skill floor of war thunder is high, and the skill ceiling even higher. Even if you feel like you're good at the game, you'll find yourself humbled if you play against an Esports team player. Their plane seems just that bit better, their reaction time just that bit better, but it's all because they have understood the game for far more competitive reasons and to a depth that's way greater than what casual players are willing to dedicate.

So, what about the fun? Between hour 5 to hour 2000, you don't get to have fun. The only way you get to "have some fun" in this game, is when you treat it very lightly and laugh it all off. However, it's difficult to laugh it all off when the game's economy is unforgiving, the grind is extremely long, and over time in order to actually have fun, you have to buy some sort of premium vehicle to aid in your learning curve.

Pay to win factor? You can buy some of the most powerful vehicles in the game with just money, at a ridiculous price tag that you would believe is crazy if it was a whole triple A game. 80 dollars. Only buy premiums when they are on sale, please, do yourself that favor. If you plan on buying a premium to grind, I would recommend the: F-18 premiums, the Su-30 premiums, and the BMPT, as those are vehicles that will minimize your suffering and maximize the suffering of others. War thunder is a fair market after all, you having fun means others will lose it.

So why would I ever play this game? The dopamine addiction and the feeling of progress. "target destroyed" sound, is an "A" note. A very satisfying sound that you'll begin to get clicker trained on. The game is difficult enough you feel proud of yourself when you actually do well and wants to play more. Your favorite vehicles are just out of reach, why wouldn't you keep going? The fear of missing out in this game is what drives it so far, and why it has so many grinding players.

Is this game any good? In my personal opinion, yes. There's nothing that feels like war thunder out there, and it feels like the controls of the game are extremely well polished. Damage is modeled relatively well and it feels pretty good to play. The game does gets problems once in a while with gaijin making weird changes that are unpolished into the game but it usually gets fixed, so it's not really that big of a concern.

How is the balancing of the game? As of currently, it's "okay". The whole game suffers a lot from BR compression, that is, vehicles that have extremely big capability differences face each other. Matchmaking in WT works by having a full up or downtier limit of 3 BR brackets. Ex: If you have a 4.0 vehicle, your full uptier is 5.0 and full downtier is 3.0. The brackets are: 4.3, 4.7, 5.0. 3 brackets, as I talked about. However vehicles that are just a bit better than another vehicle is given a 1 BR bracket bump, and as vehicles with better and better capabilities stack on top of each other, those 3 BR brackets start to feel rather suffocating. Common examples of poor balancing is the 13.3 SU-30 premiums having 8x fox-3 missiles while everyone at 13.0 either doesn't have any or have 4 fox-3s at max (if you're a really bad airframe). The Spitfire Mk.24, J6K1, as well as a bunch of 6.7 battle rating prop planes will face at 7.7, the Me-262 C2b, which is a jet aircraft with two rocket boosters that basically triple its normal jet thrust. Completely impossible to touch by those prop planes unless the jet player plays it really poorly. This is just the Air RB situation, and ground from what I heard is even worse. However you eventually learn to cope with it, though it's not good, doesn't mean it's impossible to adapt to.

Finally I want to point out that this game is NOT free to play. You either pay with money, or you pay with your soul... as for me, I paid with both. Before you start playing this game you should consider some other significantly easier to get into, and much more fun and relaxing games that does not cause this much financial pressure and frustration. It's simply not "worth your time".

If you wanna play your favorite jets, may I refer you to "Project Wingman", if you want something with a high skill ceiling but is still super fun to play, may I refer you to "Ultrakill", if you want a vehicle simulator similar to war thunder but without a significant part of the pain, may I refer you to "IL-2 Shturmovik", If you're a big fan of mil-sim combat, may I refer you to "Arma III", and if you are a real hardcore flight sim enjoyer, may I point you to "DCS World". For every aspect of this game that it offers there is one that does it just a bit better that's easier to get into.

As for me... why do I still play it? Because I already have so many hours in it, I finally got ahead of the curve. I'm finally having fun, but it's never as fun as the first innocent arcade battles can offer... Do you think it's worth it? I believe for most people the answer will be "no", but if it is worthwhile for you, be my guest and please contribute to my 14 thousand air targets destroyed when I meet you in a match one day.

Ich liebe dieses Spiel. Ich hasse dieses Spiel. Und verdammt noch mal, ich werde morgen wieder spielen.
War Thunder hat meine Seele gefressen, mein Erstgeborenes geopfert und meine Lebenszeit in einen Forschungsbaum verwandelt, der länger ist als meine verbleibende Geduld. Emotional bin ich ein Wrack, physisch ein Totalschaden und finanziell vermutlich ärmer als ein frisch gespawnter Panzer ohne Ersatzfahrzeuge. Die Gegner sind entweder Militärgenies mit gottgleicher Zielgenauigkeit oder irgendwelche Wahnsinnigen, die mich durch drei Wälder, zwei Berge und meine gesamte Existenz hindurch abschießen. Meine Granaten hingegen prallen an allem ab, was nicht aus Pappe besteht.
Und meine arschgefickten Bastarde von Teamkameraden? Ich schwöre, manchmal helfen die dem gegnerischen Team mehr als ihrem eigenen. Sie blockieren meine Schüsse, fahren mir in die Seite und beobachten seelenruhig, wie ich von drei Gegnern auseinandergenommen werde. Ich brauche keine Feinde mehr. Ich habe bereits ein ganzes Team davon.
Ich bin nur noch wenige Niederlagen davon entfernt, klassifizierte militärische Dokumente leaken zu wollen, um zu beweisen, dass meine Granate verdammt noch mal hätte penetrieren müssen. Gaijin, gebt mir Forschungspunkte, funktionierende Treffermechaniken und Teamkameraden mit mehr als zwei Gehirnzellen, bevor ich endgültig den Verstand verliere.
Und trotzdem liebe ich die Fahrzeuge, die Details und diese eine perfekte Runde, die mich vergessen lässt, dass ich gerade 47 Minuten meines Lebens und meine gesamte Würde verloren habe.
War Thunder ist keine Freizeitbeschäftigung. Es ist Stockholm-Syndrom mit Premium-Account.
Ich hasse dieses Spiel mit jeder Faser meines Körpers und liebe es mit jeder verbliebenen Gehirnzelle.
Morgen bin ich wieder online.
Ich muss noch ein Fahrzeug freischalten.
